Ten steps from a model written as syntax to a tested, constrained and extracted
mediation result. It sits between [the five-minute quickstart](native-quickstart.html)
and [the native engine guide](native-guide.html). The native engine is experimental.

| | |
|---|---|
| **You need** | medfit 0.8.0 or later (step 9 needs 0.9.0 or later, and step 10 the development version, 0.11.0); the bundled `mediation_demo` data |
| **You get** | a `SEMFit`, a test of the indirect effect, a constrained comparison, a `MediationData` |
| **Time** | about 20 minutes |

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
```

## Step 1. Write the model

One statement per line. `name * variable` labels a path, and `:=` defines a
quantity computed from labels:

```{r}
#| label: syntax
syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1
  ab := a * b
"
```

Check: the labels `a`, `b` and `cp` are the three paths; `ab` is the indirect
effect.

## Step 2. Fit it

```{r}
#| label: fit
fit <- fit_sem(syntax, mediation_demo)
fit
```

Check: `Converged: Yes`, and `ab` appears with a standard error.

## Step 3. Read the estimates

```{r}
#| label: read
tidy(fit, conf_int = TRUE)[, c("term", "estimate", "std_error", "conf_low", "conf_high")]
```

`confint(fit)` gives the same intervals on their own. Parameter names follow
lavaan: a label if you gave one, otherwise `lhs~rhs`, `X~~X` for a variance and
`eta=~m2` for a loading.

## Step 4. Check the fit

```{r}
#| label: glance
glance(fit)[, c("npar", "df", "chisq", "p_value", "AIC", "BIC")]
```

A model with no restriction has 0 degrees of freedom, so there is nothing to
reject yet. Step 6 adds a restriction and a test.

## Step 5. Test the indirect effect

The product `a * b` is zero if either factor is, so a plain test of `ab` is
unreliable. `mbco_sem()` refits with `a == 0` and with `b == 0` and uses the
smaller likelihood-ratio statistic:

```{r}
#| label: mbco
mbco_sem(fit, "a", "b")
```

## Step 6. Constrain a path and compare

Add a line to the syntax. Setting the direct effect equal to the indirect
effect is a nonlinear constraint:

```{r}
#| label: constrain
tied <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "cp == a * b\n"), mediation_demo)
round(coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")], 3)
anova(tied, fit)
```

`anova()` refits nothing; it compares the two fits' chi-squares. A large
p-value means the data do not reject the restriction.

## Step 7. A chain of three paths

For a serial model, the indirect effect is a product of three paths, and
`mbco_sem()` takes all of them:

```{r}
#| label: chain
chain <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  mediator2 ~ d * mediator1 + treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator2 + mediator1 + treatment
"
mbco_sem(fit_sem(chain, mediation_demo), paths = c("a", "d", "b"))
```

## Step 8. Get the usual mediation object

```{r}
#| label: extract
x <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                       outcome = "outcome")
tidy(x, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
```

From here `nie()`, `confint()` and `bootstrap_mediation()` work as on any other
fit.

## Step 9. Fix exogenous covariates

Needs medfit 0.9.0 or later. With many covariates, most parameters are the
exogenous variances and covariances (and the means, when the model has a mean
structure). `fixed_x = TRUE` fixes them at their sample values, as lavaan's
`fixed.x = TRUE` does, and leaves the structural paths alone. The restricted
model of Step 6 shows that the test does not move either:

```{r}
#| label: fixed-x
tied_fx <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "cp == a * b\n"), mediation_demo, fixed_x = TRUE)
round(coef(tied_fx)[c("a", "b", "cp")], 3)
rbind(
  free  = glance(tied)[, c("npar", "df", "chisq", "logLik", "fixed_x")],
  fixed = glance(tied_fx)[, c("npar", "df", "chisq", "logLik", "fixed_x")]
)
```

Check: `a`, `b` and `cp` match Step 6, and `df` and `chisq` are the same, but
`npar` is smaller. The log likelihood is conditional on the fixed variables, so
it is not comparable with the free fit's, and `anova()` refuses to compare the
two fits. `fixed_x` also takes a character vector, such as
`fixed_x = "covariate1"`, to fix only some of the exogenous variables.

## Step 10. Add a categorical covariate

Needs the development version (0.11.0). A covariate that is a factor, character or
logical column goes into the syntax by name; the engine replaces it with one 0/1 dummy
per non-reference level. The bundled data has no factor, so the chunk cuts
`covariate1` into three groups first:

```{r}
#| label: factor
dat10 <- transform(mediation_demo,
                   group = cut(covariate1, c(-Inf, -0.5, 0.5, Inf), labels = c("low", "mid", "high")))
syntax10 <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + group
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + group
  ab := a * b
"
fit10 <- fit_sem(syntax10, dat10)
tidy(fit10)[1:7, c("term", "estimate", "std_error")]
```

Check: `group` is gone from the rows, replaced by `group_mid` and `group_high`, each read
against the reference level `low` (the first factor level). `a`, `b` and `ab` keep their
usual meaning, and `mbco_sem(fit10, paths = c("a", "b"))` tests the indirect effect as in
Step 5. A label goes on one dummy (`z * group_mid`), never on `group` itself. The
[categorical covariates page](model-native-factors.html) covers constraints, missing
values, products and the four-way decomposition.
